mechanism_narrative: The current extremely depressed levels of RETAIL_REC, hovering near historical lows, indicate a floor has been reached. Any minor behavioral adaptation or slight easing of informal restrictions will lead to a marginal but positive recovery in RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than or equal to the mean of the last 28 days, indicating no recovery from the floor.

mechanism_narrative: Sustained high RESIDENTIAL mobility indicates continued adherence to stay-at-home behaviors. A significant and sustained drop in RESIDENTIAL mobility, signaling people venturing out, will directly translate to increased RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 32.0% for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not increase despite RESIDENTIAL falling below 32.0% for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated, albeit small, recovery in both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility indicates a gradual return to commuting and daily routines. This combined increase in movement will drive a positive change in RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks as more people are out and about.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both increase week-on-week for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not increase, even if WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both show consecutive week-on-week increases.

evidence_refs: fact:current severe mobility restrictions implied by data
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days does not increase despite clear signals of policy easing or public perception of reduced restrictions.

failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not decrease, even if GROCERY_PHARM falls below -55.0% for two consecutive weeks.

failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days does not increase, despite PARKS showing consecutive week-on-week increases of more than 1.0 point.
